problem_type: CLA signature persistence blocked by protected branch
symptom: A fork contributor could post the exact CLA signature comment and receive an all-signed comment, while the CLA status later failed and the contributor was absent from the persisted signature ledger.
direct_cause: The CLA action was configured to commit signatures directly to main, whose protection rules require every change to arrive through a pull request.
class_root: Mutable automation-owned state shared the protected code branch without a contract separating bot append-only storage from reviewed product source changes.
affected_population: First-time contributors signing the CLA from fork pull requests
Maintainers reviewing a misleading all-signed comment after signature persistence failed
Future contributors whose CLA status depends on signatures that never reached the durable ledger
entry_points: pull_request_target opened and synchronize events that validate all pull request commit authors
issue_comment signature commands that append a contributor to the ledger
issue_comment recheck commands that re-read the durable ledger
pull_request_target closed events that finalize the CLA conversation

external_sources.purpose: The action's official configuration explicitly states that the signature storage branch must not be protected and documents branch-based signature persistence.

invariants: Every contributor-assistant step stores signatures only on the dedicated cla-signatures branch, never on main or another protected code branch.
The code branch does not retain a second signatures/cla.json copy that can drift from the automation-owned ledger.
The CLA workflow runs from pull_request_target and issue_comment with only the permissions required to update statuses, pull-request comments, actions, and the dedicated ledger.
Fork pull request code is never checked out or executed by the privileged CLA workflow.

recurrence.reason: Every first-time fork contributor can reach the same protected-branch write, so the failure repeats until signature storage is separated from reviewed code.
same_class_scan: Parsed every workflow for contributor-assistant ownership and confirmed there is exactly one signature writer.
Queried branch protection for main and cla-signatures and verified only the dedicated ledger branch is writable by the action.
Searched the code branch for duplicate signatures/cla.json ledgers that could drift from the automation-owned source of truth.

prevention.strategy: Separate append-only automation state from protected source code and enforce that boundary in the required contracts gate.

migration: Create cla-signatures from the pre-fix main commit so the existing signedContributors history is preserved, then remove signatures/cla.json from main and point the action at the dedicated branch. Existing signature comments are reprocessed with recheck after deployment; no signature is fabricated or manually inserted.
residual_risks: The dedicated branch must remain writable by the repository GITHUB_TOKEN; adding branch protection there requires an explicit replacement storage design.
The third-party action can still emit a misleading comment before a later write error; durable ledger content and the final check conclusion remain the acceptance evidence.
